To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in the dipolar regime, the dynamo bifucation is supercritical, (ii) in a bistable regime, dipolar and non-dipolar dynamos co-exist, (iii) in a bistability regime, the dynamical properties of dipolar dynamos are different from those of non-dipolar ones, (iv) in the turbulent flow regime (Ra/ Rac>10), Lorentz force affects significantly the dynamics of dynamos.
(i) the dynamo bifucation depends on the initial field, and (ii) the dynamo threshold is significantly affected by the initial magnetic field and by the flow structure.

(i) the transition between dipole-dominated and multipolar dynamo solutions in spherical shells is not abrupt but is replaced by a bistable region, (ii) this bistability is due to the development of zonal flows in the turbulent regime and (iii) the Lorentz forces affect significantly the flow structure when the dynamo is far above the threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamical properties of the transition between dipolar and multipole dynamos.
the nature of the bifurcating solutions of the geodynamo problem.
the dynamo bifucation in spherical shells with no-slip boundary conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dipolar field topology is the result of a competition between the magnetic and viscous forces and is therefore not a direct consequence of the dynamical regime.
the Earth’s core has been in a bistable state during the last 3.5 Ga.
, in the Earth’s core, the dipole field may not be the most efficient field to sustain a dynamo, but it is the most stable one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dipole field can be considered as a secondary bifurcation of a turbulent flow, with a supercritical bifurcation.
the dynamo transition is a complex and multi-parameter process.

, in a configuration with no-slip conditions and with Ekman number of the order of 10-5, the dynamo bifucation can occur in three different ways: (i) supercritical, (ii) subcritical and (iii) bistable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given set of parameters, the dynamo bifucation can be either supercritical or subcritical depending on whether the magnetic field is weak or strong.

the dipole-dominated dynamo branch is the only one that can be reached from an initial state without magnetic field, and that the multipolar branch can only be reached by starting the simulation from a magnetic field with a sufficiently large amplitude.
the dynamo transition is more complex than previously believed and that the dipole field is a secondary phenomenon in the turbulent regime.
